answer: Ask the ivory first: it tells you whether the work was ever done at all. Proof of pewter caster mould via pewterers company works that way — a mould the pewterers company files only after the caster pours a dish he actually cast. A claimant who never touched the craft must still produce the mark, and forging one costs the forger 11 days of bench time plus 11 pieces of stock he cannot sell. The orchard is the second check: it carries the maker's stamp, and a stamped prism with no maker behind it is worth less than the wood it was cut from.
